context: Two coworkers debrief after a tense meeting
purpose: Teach: おかしく/怒っ/本音/癖/救い/なくなる/怪しい/熱く

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: さっきの会議、部長がやけに怒ってたな。
lines.en: The director was unusually angry in that meeting earlier.
lines.style: Tense post-meeting opener, weary masculine office tone.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 本当に。途中から話がおかしくなって、私もどうしようかと思った。
lines.en: Seriously. The conversation went off the rails partway through and I didn't know what to do.
lines.style: Sympathetic feminine reply, exhaling relief after stress.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: あの人、追い詰められると早口になる癖があるんだよ。
lines.en: That guy has a habit of talking fast when he gets cornered.
lines.style: Observational masculine analysis, slightly amused undertone.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 唯一の救いは、佐藤さんが間に入ってくれたことかな。
lines.en: The one saving grace was probably that Sato-san stepped in between them.
lines.style: Reflective feminine gratitude, lowering voice cautiously.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 確かに。あのまま続いてたら、誰かの居場所がなくなるところだった。
lines.en: True. If it had kept going, someone's position here would've been gone.
lines.style: Grave masculine agreement, half-joking but genuinely worried.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 数字の説明も怪しいところが多くて、誰も突っ込めない空気で。
lines.en: There were a lot of fishy spots in the number explanations too, but the atmosphere made it impossible to push back.
lines.style: Lowered feminine whisper, conspiratorial workplace gossip tone.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 課長が熱く語り始めた時点で、もう本音は聞けないって思ったよ。
lines.en: The moment the section chief started passionately lecturing, I figured we wouldn't hear anyone's real thoughts.
lines.style: Resigned masculine sigh, jaded middle-manager perspective tone.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: とりあえず、コーヒーでも飲んで気持ち切り替えましょう。
lines.en: For now, let's grab some coffee and reset our mood.
lines.style: Warm feminine recovery suggestion, gently steering away.
